transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. I work as a loan officer, and lately... I'll just stare at a loan worksheet or my client follow-up list and reread the same line over and over again. Then I end up putting off making my calls, mostly because even simple decisions just feel a lot harder than they should right now.
Over the past few weeks, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or down most of the time?

Yes, I have been feeling pretty down. Most days, actually. There's just this... dull heaviness that kind of sits with me. Even when I try to do things I usually enjoy, like going to the community center or working out in my garden, places that really used to lift my spirits... I just feel like I'm going through the motions. I'll have a smile pasted on for everyone else, but that heaviness is still there.

Have you experienced any recent illnesses, injuries, or changes in medications—either new prescriptions or stopping something you were taking—around the time these concentration problems and low mood started?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or had any kind of injury. And... no, my medications haven't changed at all. I haven't started anything new or stopped taking anything. Physically, everything has been pretty much exactly the same as usual.
Have you experienced any sudden episodes where you felt a rush of intense fear or anxiety, even when there didn't seem to be an obvious reason for it?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, I worry about things sometimes, sure, but I've never had a sudden rush of fear or panic out of nowhere. It's really just the low mood and the trouble focusing that I mentioned.
When you think about your day-to-day life, do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things—like work, finances, your health, or relationships—even when there's no immediate problem?

No, I wouldn't say I worry a lot. I mean, as a loan officer, I see people's financial troubles all day, so I think about money and the economy, but it doesn't keep me up at night or make me anxious. I don't really worry about my health or relationships either. Like I said, it's more of just a constant feeling of being down, not really a nervous or worried feeling.
How long have you been feeling this way—this low mood and trouble concentrating? Can you think back to when it started?
It's been a long time. I guess... well, this has been going on since my close friend died. That was a little over two years ago now. It just seems like I've felt this way ever since then.
When your friend first died two years ago, did you start feeling this heaviness and trouble concentrating right away, or did it develop gradually over weeks or months after that?

I think it started pretty much right away. I mean, obviously, I was grieving at first, so I was really sad then. But that heavy feeling just... never lifted. It just kind of settled in right after it happened and stayed there.

In those two years since your friend passed away, has this heavy feeling and difficulty concentrating been pretty much constant, or have there been times when you felt noticeably better for a while before it came back?
No, it's been pretty constant. I haven't really had any periods where I felt noticeably better. It's just been this same heavy, low feeling day in and day out for the whole two years.

When you think about your friend who passed away, do you find yourself mainly missing them and wishing they were still here, or has your low mood become more about feeling hopeless or empty about life in general, even beyond just missing your friend?

I still miss her, of course. But... I think it's definitely become more about everything else now. I keep telling myself that things might turn around eventually, but underneath that, I just have this really tired feeling. It just feels like this is how my life is going to be from now on—just smaller and harder, no matter what I try.
